newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican crude port Pajaritos reopens to exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican crude port Pajaritos reopens to exports.

text.p: Mexican crude port Pajaritos reopened Thursday at 0700 local/1200 GMT as the weather improved, a port official said.
He told Reuters 28 ships were waiting to load and sail, and at least 16 of the tankers were of state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
Storms in the Gulf of Mexico closed Mexico's three main crude ports last weekend. Pajaritos in Veracruz state reopened after a five-day closure that backed up crude tankers.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened at 0800 as winds and waves also relaxed. The nation's largest crude port, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, reopened early Monday.
Port officials said delayed crude shipments will be sent out as soon as possible.
Pajaritos shipped an average 416,200 barrels per day (bpd) of crude in 1996, Dos Bocas shipped about 505,900 bpd and Cayo Arcas shipped 576,300 bpd, according to the latest Pemex figures.
